1. DESCRIPTION
The Department of Veterans Affairs, VA Long Beach Healthcare System (VALBHS)Â is conducting market research to identify qualified businesses capable of providing comprehensive preventive maintenance, repair, software maintenance, commissioning, and technical support services for the facility s existing Johnson Controls Metasys Building Automation System (BAS) and four YORK centrifugal chillers.
The purpose of this notice is to determine the availability and capability of potential sources, including small businesses and eligible Veteran-Owned Small Businesses (VOSBs) and Service-Disabled Veteran-Owned Small Businesses (SDVOSBs), to perform the required services.
Information obtained through this notice will assist the Government in determining the appropriate acquisition strategy.


2. REQUIREMENT
The VA Long Beach Healthcare System requires comprehensive maintenance and technical support services for its existing Johnson Controls Metasys BAS and four YORK centrifugal chillers.
The contractor shall provide all necessary personnel, supervision, equipment, tools, materials, replacement parts, technical expertise, and other resources required to perform preventive maintenance, inspections, troubleshooting, repairs, software support, and emergency services.
The anticipated scope of work includes, but is not limited to:
Existing Proprietary System Environment
The required services shall be performed on the Government s existing Johnson Controls Metasys Building Automation System and associated YORK centrifugal chillers. The installed Metasys system monitors and controls critical and non-critical mechanical equipment, including temperature, humidity, pressure, critical alarms, and equipment notifications supporting healthcare operations. The YORK chillers are integrated with and controlled through the existing Metasys system.
The Government is not seeking replacement of the existing Metasys system. Any respondent must demonstrate that it possesses, or will possess before performance begins, the legal authority, technical capability, manufacturer-level access, qualified personnel, and proprietary resources necessary to perform the complete requirement on the installed system without loss of functionality, interruption of critical facility operations, compromise of cybersecurity, or invalidation of applicable warranties.
At a minimum, the contractor must have the capability and legal authority to:
Access, diagnose, maintain, program, configure, modify, and restore the installed Metasys system and its databases, controllers, field devices, sensors, interfaces, and associated components.
Use all required proprietary or manufacturer-controlled Metasys software, service applications, programming tools, diagnostic tools, passwords, credentials, licenses, firmware, technical documentation, and update repositories.
Obtain and install current, authorized Metasys software updates, firmware updates, security patches, hot fixes, and compatible replacement components throughout the period of performance.
Service legacy Metasys controllers, sensors, and field devices currently installed at the facility, including equipment that may no longer be commercially available through ordinary distribution channels.
Maintain full interoperability between the Metasys system, YORK chillers, mechanical equipment, alarms, operator workstations, servers, databases, communications networks, and existing control sequences.
Perform work without disabling, bypassing, or degrading existing safety functions, environmental controls, monitoring capabilities, alarms, notifications, cybersecurity controls, or system integrations.
Preserve all applicable equipment, software, and system warranties and avoid unauthorized system changes that could impair warranty coverage.
Provide manufacturer-authorized or equivalently qualified technicians trained and experienced in the installed Metasys architecture and YORK centrifugal chillers.
Coordinate software changes and security-patch activities with Government facility and information-technology personnel to avoid introducing cybersecurity vulnerabilities or disrupting critical healthcare operations.
Obtain authorized original equipment manufacturer replacement parts and components necessary to maintain system compatibility and functionality.
